payload.comment:
Profiling stage is structurally sound and internally consistent. All arithmetic checks pass: class counts sum to official split sizes (train 89996, val 10004, test 7180); proportions, imbalance ratios, and test-to-train prevalence ratios are correctly computed. No duplicates, no blank images, 100 % of data profiled, all three index SHA-256 hashes and the archive MD5 are present, and the code SHA-256 is recorded. The dataset is pathmnist (28×28×3, 9 classes), which is a very low-resolution histopathology benchmark; this is an inherent limitation, not a profiling error.

Carried-forward concerns that must be tracked in every downstream stage:

1. LLM reproducibility gap (from ingestion, still unresolved): llm_model_digest is null while qwen3.8 via ollama is declared. Exact weights are unpinned. The name 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen family; verify it resolves to the intended checkpoint. Until a digest or full registry identifier is recorded, any LLM-dependent step is not fully reproducible.

2. Test-domain shift: CRC-VAL-HE-7K originates from a different clinical center. Class-prevalence ratios deviate substantially (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56), and the test imbalance ratio (3.95) is more than double the train ratio (1.63). All downstream evaluation must report in-domain (train/val) and cross-domain (test) metrics separately and label the test set as external.

3. Label ambiguity at 28×28: 'debris' is non-standard and overlaps with 'mucus'/'background'; 'cancer-associated stroma' vs 'smooth muscle' and 'normal colon mucosa' vs 'adenocarcinoma epithelium' are visually confusable without architectural context. No inter-annotator-agreement data is provided for the external center. Per-class test counts for debris (339), stroma (421), and smooth muscle (592) are small enough that per-class F1/accuracy will be statistically noisy; report confidence intervals.

4. Train/val near-identical distribution (max Δ < 0.001) confirms a random split of a single-site dataset; the only true generalization probe is the skewed external test set, which conflates distribution shift with domain shift.

None of these are profiling errors; they are dataset-level risks that are correctly identified and documented. The profiling artefact is complete and accurate. Proceed to the next stage, ensuring the above caveats are propagated into training, evaluation, and reporting configurations.
